headline: Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant

sources: Plant management Telegram post, relayed by Reuters (https://www.reuters.com/world/driver-russian-held-zaporizhzhia-nuclear-plant-killed-drone-attacks-managers-say-2026-10-21/)
fault_line: Deliberate targeting of nuclear-plant staff transport vs fog-of-war claim from an interested party — who is endangering Europe's largest nuclear plant, and where is the IAEA?

sections.what_happened: Management at the Russian-held Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant (Europe's largest, six reactors) said a driver at the station was killed on Wednesday after two days of Ukrainian drone attacks. Buses carrying staff to and from the plant 'had come under attack for two days in a row.' Statement: 'The second straight day of attacks on the station's transport shows that these strikes are deliberate'; attacks 'pose a direct threat' to staff who ensure operations at the plant. Context in same Reuters piece: Rosatom said last week an IAEA-mediated truce agreement was in place to allow repairs at a thermal power station supplying power to the plant; Rosatom also said a July Ukrainian drone attack on a service car killed the plant's chief engineer and the vehicle's driver.
sections.what_verified: Reuters wire carried by Devdiscourse, Mezha, multiple US radio-station syndication sites (wixx, yall1067, froggyweb, hot96, ktwb, kwsn) — all the same wire, no independent second source. The claim that management SAID it is confirmed; the underlying event (driver killed by Ukrainian drones) rests solely on the Russian-held management's Telegram post.
sections.what_disputed: No Ukrainian official response found; no IAEA statement yet on this specific killing. Both sides have repeatedly accused each other of activity jeopardising nuclear safety; Russia has in recent months accused Ukraine of attacking plant-linked sites including transport. The interested-party origin (Russian-held management) must be carried as attribution, never as confirmed fact.
sections.why_matters: Two days of drone strikes on staff buses at Europe's largest nuclear plant — the moment a war of attrition touches the nuclear tripwire. Carry the IAEA lifeline frame: off-site power is the plant's survival margin, and it is already under a negotiated truce that the strikes are shredding. Editorial note: the Russian-held management is an interested party — attribute the 'deliberate' claim, do not adopt it.
sections.context: Background: ELEVATION — Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant: driver killed after two days of drone attacks on staff transport; plant management calls strikes 'deliberate' (Reuters, Oct 21/22)
